notes: owner 2026-11-20 (spec 2026-11-20-heavy-infantry-arm-design, Opening regiments; first draft): every kingdom opens with units_min..units_max regiments of this arm, written by tools/army_starts.gd for tools/import_azgaar.gd. COUNT: kingdoms ranked by military/kingdoms.csv strength before these regiments (ties by code); the upper half (an odd middle one counts upper) takes units_max, the rest units_min. SIZE (share_permille 0): a kingdom's average is avg_strongest for the strongest (men_max x 0.9) and avg_weakest for the weakest (men_min x 1.1), linear in strength between; the regiment at its largest town is one men_step above the average, the last one men_step below, the others the average; each rounded half up to men_step and clamped to men_min..men_max. PLACE largest_towns: the kingdom's towns (political/burgs.csv) by population, largest first, ties by code, one regiment each, and when it has fewer towns than regiments the rest at its largest town again; a regiment stands at its town's position in the town's province, and while any regiment already written (the export's or an earlier one of these) stands nearer than offset_km it moves out offset_km at a time along `bearings` (degrees, 0 east, 90 south in the pack's y-down frame), each ring k = 1, 2, ... trying every bearing in order before the next; with in_province 1 a ring spot outside the town's own province (the pack's province index) is passed over. CODE <kingdom>_<ordinal>_<code_word>_<town>, LABEL '<ordinal> (<Town>) <label_word>'

owner 2026-11-26 (spec 2026-11-26-militia-arm-design, Opening regiments; first draft): COUNT, PLACE, CODE and LABEL as the row above. SIZE (share_permille > 0, the SHARE rule; avg_* unread): ARMY = the men of the kingdom's non-naval regiments already written when this row runs (the export's and the rows above's: rules run in file order); TOTAL T = max(army x share_permille / 1000, total_min) rounded half up to men_step; base = T / n (n its regiment count) rounded half up to men_step; the regiment at its largest town is one men_step above the base, the last one men_step below, the others the base; each clamped to men_min..men_max. total_min is the least a kingdom's total may be before the clamp (the smallest regiment the export writes). PLACE: ring_from is the first ring tried (0 the town's point, the row above's): these start at ring 2 of offset_km 1, so 2 km out and then 3, clear of the others by 1 km. That keeps every one inside a large town's reach (data/army/army_town_reach.csv) and its own province (every land regiment opens in a town its kingdom holds, owner 2026-10-06), and never the regiment nearest a capital's point (ArmySplit takes the king's household from that one)
